leads.name: Kauri Pine (City Botanic Gardens)

location.neighbourhood: City Botanic Gardens, south east of the formal flower garden

leads.why_not_verified: National Trust database only (Alice_Street_5): planted 1980, only roughly 45 years old. Too young to be a strong ancient-tree candidate; parked rather than pursued.

leads.name: Anzac (Turkish) Pines (City Botanic Gardens)

location.neighbourhood: City Botanic Gardens, eastern side near the George Street / Parliament House entrance

leads.why_not_verified: Planted 26 April 1979 from seed brought back from Lone Pine, Gallipoli, by veteran soldiers; historically significant (Anzac commemoration) but a group of 5 trees (2 originals plus 3 later replacements after 2 died), each only roughly 46 years old and modest (8m tall). Not pursued this pass: unclear whether it passes the single-collectible-point test given it is a small planted group with a mixed-age replacement history, and the age/size are both slight. Worth a judgement call by a future pass rather than a default no.

blocked.name: Weeping Fig Avenue (City Botanic Gardens, eastern river path)

location.neighbourhood: City Botanic Gardens, eastern river path from the Edward Street entrance

blocked.reason: National Trust database (Alice_Street_13) explicitly describes this as an 'Avenue' of 9 trees planted by head gardener James Pink (1881-1886) along the riverbank, distinct from the already-published pair at the Alice Street gate (bne_009, a different National Trust entry, 147_Alice_Street_6). Not a single collectible point, same reasoning as the already-blocked Bunya Pine Avenue; never ship as one entry.

blocked.name: Bunya Pine Avenue (City Botanic Gardens)
blocked.reason: Not a single collectible point. Row of roughly 18 mature Bunya Pines planted by Walter Hill 1858-1867, skirting several hundred metres of the eastern river walk from inside the Edward Street entrance. Well documented (National Trust database: trusttrees.org.au/tree/QLD/Brisbane/Brisbane_City_Botanic_Gardens_Alice_Street_8; State Library of Queensland blog; Wikipedia calls it explicitly 'an avenue of bunya pines') but per the verify-pass rule an avenue is blocked regardless of fame or documentation quality. If a single standout specimen within the row is ever individually distinguished by a source (e.g. the largest or first-planted), it could be lifted out as its own entry.

note:
Brisbane City Council's 558-record significant/landscape tree overlay (data/registers/brisbane-significant-landscape-trees.json) carries NO species, name, age or vitality field, only a designation polygon centroid; it does not by itself clear the two-source bar for any tree and none of it was directly usable this pass without a named tree to match it to. Checked distance from each of the 8 verified City Botanic Gardens/Eagle Street trees to the nearest of the 558 overlay points: nearest was 520m (Eagle Street Fig Trees) and 535-745m for the Botanic Gardens trees, i.e. none of the overlay's individually-designated points sit close enough to plausibly be the same tree, so the overlay was not cited as a source for any of the 8. A future pass with more time could try to match named significant trees elsewhere in Brisbane (New Farm Park, Roma Street Parkland, Mount Coot-tha Botanic Gardens, university campuses) against the overlay's remaining ~550 unmatched points to grow a second cluster; this pass stayed inside the single City Botanic Gardens / Eagle Street cluster (max pairwise distance 1.12km) per the brief's preference for a dense walkable cluster over scattered candidates.

2026-08-23 DEEPEN PASS UPDATE: the 4 priority candidates (Silky Oak, Hoop Pine, second Big-leaf Mahogany, Black Bean) were pursued this pass and delivered to data/research/brisbane-verified.json as bne_012 through bne_015, each with National Trust's own plotted tree-level coordinates (confirmed precision) and girth derived from the register's diameter field. None cleared the two-independent-source bar: an extensive second-source search (Wikipedia's City Botanic Gardens and Brisbane City Botanic Gardens articles, the SLQ blog on the NT Significant Tree app, brisbanebotanictreasures.info live and via Wayback across three of its sub-pages, the National Register of Big Trees, and nearby iNaturalist observations for each species) found nothing naming any of the four specific trees. Delivered anyway per the project's single-source rule, each with curation_status flagged and a verify_notes explanation. brisbanebotanictreasures.info now hangs completely on a live fetch (curl -m 15 times out connecting to the bare domain root, 202.37.74.45); added to data/fetch-blocklist.json. The Black Bean's 1951 Speaker's Chair anecdote (flagged in the original lead as worth confirming) does NOT hold for this specific tree: it was only about 7 years old in 1951, per its own recorded ~1944 planting date, so it could not have supplied the carving timber; National Trust's text describes the species/historical gift generally, not this specimen. The Kauri Pine and Anzac Pines leads below were not revisited this pass (out of the 4-candidate budget) and remain open.
